baselineAudit.notes: Static triage only. 40/244 items in the third rewrite tranche have been classified for substantive revision and qualified educator review; no clinical approval or content change was recorded.

commonFindings: Repeated generic reassessment stem skeleton across all 20 items.
Only four generic option-family templates were reused across the 20 items (five items per family).
Rationales repeat generic escalation/assessment/effectiveness wording and frequently do not support the named topic or CJMM function.
Maternal/newborn labels are repeatedly paired with adult/child demographics or without pregnancy, labor, birth, or postpartum context.
High-risk vital signs and laboratory findings recur across unrelated topics without a coherent patient record.

findings: Placenta-previa topic is paired with a 3-day-old newborn; no maternal pregnancy/bleeding/placental-location context.
Oliguria and hyperkalemia with peaked T waves do not establish placenta previa; generic escalation choices and rationale are not topic-specific.
Uterine inversion is presented in a 56-year-old without childbirth/postpartum context.
Hypotension/tachycardia may indicate instability, but INR elevation and gross hematuria do not establish inversion; answer choices and rationale are generic.
Postpartum hypertension lacks a clear pregnancy/postpartum timeline and does not present hypertension; fever, hypotension, severe hyponatremia and seizure dominate the stem.
Generic communication options do not test recognition or management of postpartum hypertension.
Newborn age is plausible for jaundice, but no bilirubin value, age-in-hours, gestational age, hemolysis risk or feeding context is supplied.
Hypercapnia and somnolence suggest a different acute problem; outcome/effectiveness options do not match the stated take-action function.
Newborn respiratory distress is assigned to a 22-year-old adult with dizziness and bradycardia.
Hypoglycemia/inability to swallow is not a neonatal respiratory assessment; no newborn respiratory signs or perinatal context are present.
Meconium aspiration is assigned to a 68-year-old admitted from home, without birth or neonatal respiratory context.
Oliguria and hypoglycemia are not sufficient evidence for the named respiratory condition; generic priority choices are reused.
Neonatal sepsis is assigned to a 7-year-old child, contradicting the neonatal label.
Hypotension and thrombocytopenia are nonspecific without neonatal/infectious timeline or focused cues; generic options/rationale do not resolve the mismatch.
Group B streptococcal prophylaxis is assigned to a 79-year-old with no pregnancy, labor, screening, allergy or intrapartum timing context.
Hypoxemia and falling hemoglobin are unrelated to the prophylaxis decision; options test response evaluation rather than prophylaxis.
Labor analgesia safety is assigned to a 68-year-old admitted from home with no labor, neuraxial procedure or analgesic exposure context.
Confusion, elevated lactate and rising creatinine are nonspecific deterioration cues; the item does not test labor-analgesia safety.
Postpartum thromboembolism is assigned to a 7-year-old child with no postpartum context.
Severe hypertension and hyperkalemia/peaked T waves do not establish thromboembolism; no VTE-focused assessment or escalation decision is supplied.
Atrial fibrillation with rapid response lacks ECG/rhythm evidence; fever, hypotension and hyperkalemia with peaked T waves create competing acute priorities.
The generic assessment/communication options do not test rhythm recognition or a defensible AF-with-RVR decision.
Inferior STEMI lacks chest-pain characterization, ECG leads/ST findings, troponin trend or other diagnostic evidence.
INR elevation and gross hematuria are unexplained; outcome/effectiveness options do not test the stated take-action task.
Acute decompensated heart failure lacks congestion, dyspnea, oxygenation, volume-status or relevant diagnostic cues.
Bradycardia/hypotension with severe hyponatremia and seizure suggests a competing emergency; generic escalation choices do not assess heart-failure management.
Cardiac tamponade has no procedure/cardiac timeline or focused findings such as obstructive-shock pattern, venous congestion or diagnostic confirmation.
Hypercapnia and somnolence are nonspecific; generic ABC choices do not test tamponade recognition or response.
Pulmonary embolism is assigned to a 3-day-old newborn without neonatal thrombotic risk or respiratory presentation.
Hypertension and hypoglycemia do not establish PE; no oxygenation, perfusion or diagnostic context is given.
Proximal DVT lacks unilateral limb pain/swelling, edema, circumference or venous-imaging context.
Fever, hypotension and hypoglycemia are unrelated/nonspecific; outcome/effectiveness options do not test DVT assessment or escalation.
Acute limb ischemia lacks limb-specific laterality, pulse, temperature, color, sensation, movement or capillary-refill findings.
Severe pain is paired with thrombocytopenia/bleeding rather than a coherent limb-perfusion assessment; generic escalation choices are reused.
Symptomatic sinus bradycardia is assigned to a 3-day-old newborn but uses adult-style blood pressure/dizziness and an unexplained adult-like hemoglobin trend.
No age-appropriate neonatal perfusion/context or rhythm evidence is supplied; generic prioritization choices do not address the item.
Vasospastic angina lacks episodic rest chest pain, transient ischemic ECG changes or a vasospasm-related decision point.
Oliguria, lactate elevation and rising creatinine are unrelated to the named angina topic; generic assessment/communication options are reused.
Implantable defibrillator discharge lacks shock count/timing, rhythm, symptoms, device history or post-discharge assessment.
Hypotension/tachycardia and hyperkalemia with peaked T waves create a competing arrhythmia concern; outcome/effectiveness options do not test ICD-discharge response.
